Author: rebelmike
Content:
To give some background:
TQVA/TQVB/TQVC were on run 1 and are identical designs, one in each of the quarter and half slot types. It’s a fairly minimal change over the Tiny Tapeout version, so the main IO is 8 inputs and 8 outputs (direction fixed), though UART and audio are broken out to separate pins.

I’ve proven TQVC works on a simpler host board which has the flash and RAM on a PMOD as in Tiny Tapeout. I designed a CoB for TQVA which matches the pinout of TQVC, and I believe I will very soon have 80 TQVA CoBs to test.

The design itself has peripherals for UART, SPI, PWM, SNES gamepads via the TinyTapeout PMOD, VGA out through the TinyTapeout PMOD, a couple of synths for audio, a couple of different programmable IO type blocks, and some other unusual peripherals from the Tiny Tapeout peripheral competition. It should make a decent platform for retro style games (but compiled with a modern toolchain).

Author: rebelmike
Content:
On run 2 there were two new versions of TinyQV:
TQVD has an attempt at HDMI output, giving an 80x30 text mode with a scrollable full screen buffer (no need to race the beam!). The font has 32 programmable characters. The same display driver can also output VGA. IO is more flexible, GPIO can fully configure the 16 GPIO pins.

TQVE is an experiment with only 17 pads. That means it only has 6 GPIO, but it has a lot more on board scratch RAM. It also has a USB CDC peripheral, which will hopefully allow a serial console without needing an external UART adapter.

Both TQVD and TQVE use Tholin’s new cell library

Content: I haven't been following what the plan is for the flex PCB, is the idea to bond that to the chip and then to pads on a regular PCB?  So I could just design a variant of the regular host board with a suitable pad layout for it

Author: namibj
Content:
Well, so, on the flex they come out from the die itself in the same order they are on the die, and IMO after they've left the die surface and a reasonable strain relief zone next to the right (SRAM) edge, then we can expand.
Also, the back/far layer has to be free of copper around the pads for visual alignment reasons; and IMO we might want to keep it pulled back on the entire die for starters (but not long-term).

Author: rebelmike
Content: It looks like the pad pitch on TQVE is 102um so this would be super tight - you wouldn't be able to put a pad at all on the FPC, it would just be the 2mil trace.

Author: namibj
Content: yeah, that's normal for dense ACF usage, line pitch close to process minimums on one of the two sides (whichever has more trouble with fine pitch).

Author: namibj
Content: With this limitation and assuming to put power and gnd pads in the center instead, considering those don't really need the fancy stuff from the pad ring cells, a full slot should just about manage 148 IO's _I think._

Author: namibj
Content: Relies on CUP for the power and ground in the middle in practice though, IMO. Or "ab"-using the 4 corners to feed in through one large pad each that occupies almost all the area not in the way of the pad fanout traces and between sealring and power-ring-corner-cell.

# Welcome to #🐭-tinyqv
This channel is for **TinyQV**, @RebelMike's (Mike Bell) small RISC-V SoC, first built for Tiny Tapeout, and the chips made on wafer.space runs. @RebelMike looks after this channel.

**Chips**
- Run 1: [TQVA](<https://wafer.space/ws-run1/projects/TQVA.html>), [TQVB](<https://wafer.space/ws-run1/projects/TQVB.html>) and [TQVC](<https://wafer.space/ws-run1/projects/TQVC.html>)
- Run 2: [TQVA](<https://wafer.space/ws-run2/projects/TQVA.html>), [TQVC](<https://wafer.space/ws-run2/projects/TQVC.html>), [TQVD](<https://wafer.space/ws-run2/projects/TQVD.html>) (HDMI output) and [TQVE](<https://wafer.space/ws-run2/projects/TQVE.html>) (experimental pad setup)

**Source**
- [tinyQV](<https://github.com/MichaelBell/tinyQV>): the core, for Tiny Tapeout
- [ws01-tinyQV](<https://github.com/MichaelBell/ws01-tinyQV>): Run 1
- [ws02-tinyQV](<https://github.com/MichaelBell/ws02-tinyQV>): Run 2

If you have one of these chips, please post your bring-up results, boards, firmware and questions here.
